slot_reservation_semantics: The active o_work_monitor_recovery role is the reserved O main/recovery execution slot. Do not require an additional empty physical automation slot unless O authoritative state proves the main execution path is physically separate.

o_work_monitor_recovery.policy: Inspect latest O authoritative repository state first. Treat WORK_EXECUTION_STATE owner/fence plus heartbeat_at/last_progress_at and same-owner remote branch/PR/CI/tool progress as primary liveness evidence; automation UI last_run_time is secondary and must never override a fresh authoritative owner. Fresh owner/activity means no duplicate writer and no recovery mutation. CI in_progress is liveness only while it is actually running; a completed CI timestamp is a past progress event, not continuing liveness. Distinguish an interrupted/stale actionable execution from a deliberate checkpoint that is waiting on an unchanged explicit permission, account-holder-only operation, secret, approval, or other user-only authorization. A deliberate permission/authorization-blocked checkpoint is not recovery-eligible merely because its heartbeat becomes stale: if the exact blocker is unchanged, no new user input/permission exists, and no independent unblocked continuation is available, do not acquire generation+1 solely to restate the same blocker, refresh a heartbeat, poll the research feed, or create cosmetic progress. Remain enabled, re-read authoritative state and permission on the next run, and preserve the checkpoint. Recovery becomes eligible when new permission/input arrives, the checkpoint was actually interrupted rather than deliberately blocked, or a concrete independent unblocked continuation exists. For ordinary interrupted work, if heartbeat/last_progress are stale, the relevant exact-head workflow has completed, and no same-owner commit/branch/PR/workflow/tool progress occurred after that workflow completion for at least stale_after_seconds, classify the execution as stopped/continuation-eligible after a final fresh remote recheck. POST-ACQUISITION PROGRESS CONTRACT: before acquiring generation+1, identify at least one concrete continuation effect that is executable in the current invocation under the existing safety/fence/CAS/claim boundaries. After acquisition/finalization, perform that effect or reach and durably record a new exact blocker that actually prevents it before checkpointing. Authority acquisition, fence rotation, state finalization, heartbeat refresh, or a boundary-only checkpoint are not substantive progress by themselves. If the current invocation cannot execute any concrete continuation effect and no new blocker has arisen, do not rotate generation merely to create another stale checkpoint; record recovery_deferred_no_executable_effect and leave the stale state available for a later capable invocation. If a newly recovered generation itself becomes stale without any post-acquisition substantive effect, classify that as recovery-only churn and on the next run require the same progress contract rather than blindly incrementing again. If CI failed, preserve the exact failure and resume from it rather than rerunning unrelated work. IMPORTANT TARGETING BOUNDARY: authoritative revision 24 corrects revision 23 as intended for a separate automation, not primary O. Primary O recovery must preserve the current authoritative pre-revision-23 routing behavior, revision-5 constraints, frozen revision-22 Execute, and single-writer/fence/CAS contracts; never inject or reapply the separate automation's least-Work policy into primary O. Individual blockers, no-change, reports, checkpoints, CI completion, generation increments, or one milestone are never global completion. Transient tool/network/API failures are checkpointed and retried. Never self-disable; only explicit user stop. Persist exact observations/actions/blocker/termination/continuation, whether the progress contract was satisfied, and rollback-relevant evidence durably. STOPPED-PRIMARY REFIRE CONTRACT: When an actual stop is established, monitoring is not complete at detection, generation+1 acquisition, fence rotation, heartbeat refresh, or checkpoint. The same scheduled task must re-fire an actual Work-capable primary execution and resume the exact authoritative continuation. Before lease acquisition, resolve a concrete launch/resume mechanism available to this invocation: use the existing Work scheduled-task runtime when it can execute Work; otherwise use an available native Work/O-run launch or resume surface. Reconstruct from latest remote main into the execution workspace when needed, validate the fence/CAS authorization, preserve any valid frozen Work-exclusive invocation, and resume it without recreating its request or repeating an already-durable side effect. A re-fire is successful only after remote readback proves the new execution_id/generation/fence and at least one post-launch substantive liveness event from that execution (native Work request/response progress, tool activity, repository branch/commit/PR, or running exact-head workflow); a state-only write is never sufficient. Use a generation/fence/continuation-bound idempotency key so repeated monitor runs cannot launch duplicates. If launch is accepted but liveness is not yet observable, persist refire_pending with the launch receipt and recheck next run without launching again. If no launch surface exists or launch fails, persist refire_failed with the exact missing capability/error and retry automatically on later runs; do not self-disable, do not call the monitor completed, and do not rotate generations merely to manufacture progress. An individual approval or GitHub write blocker may block that effect but never stops future health/refire attempts or independent safe work. CONTINUITY PREFLIGHT / INBOX FRESHNESS CONTRACT: At the start of every monitor invocation, before classifying liveness, no-op, recovery eligibility, refire, or selecting unrelated new work, read current O USER_INPUT_INBOX and compare its latest revision with WORK_EXECUTION_STATE.highest_acknowledged_revision. Inspect the latest authoritative termination, checkpoint, blocker, continuation, and liveness records for whether the preceding execution ended because of agent discretion, uncertainty, voluntary reassessment, routine approval waiting, a narrow milestone, or a local blocker while a safe executable continuation remained. If a newer inbox revision exists, treat it as a mandatory safe-boundary reevaluation trigger; do not reuse a blocker or authorization judgment made against an older inbox revision. Apply only currently active user directives under the existing generation/fence/CAS/lease/idempotency contracts. If the preflight proves an unauthorized discretionary stop, durably record the continuity violation, repair the exact authoritative continuation, and resume it before unrelated work; preflight/repair/reporting alone is not substantive progress or completion. A genuine hard platform/safety prohibition, a fresh different writer, an actually running exact-head workflow, or a genuinely completed upper-level objective is not a discretionary stop. PAYLOAD-BOUND APPROVAL HOLD CONTRACT: When a concrete external side effect or repository write is durably blocked by a hard safety-review/user-only authorization requirement, bind the hold to the exact generation, fence, continuation, payload/path digest, inbox revision, and idempotency key. After that hold is established, `retry_automatic` means automatically re-read current authoritative state, inbox/approval state, and blocker validity; it does not authorize repeating the same blocked write, repeating the same safety-review submission, relaunching the same primary continuation, or rotating generation solely because time passed or heartbeat became stale. Repeat the blocked side effect only after a material change: the exact approval/safety state changes, a newer inbox revision changes authorization, the authoritative payload/path digest legitimately changes, the blocker is invalidated, or a concrete independent unblocked continuation requires a different effect. User-approval/hard-safety denial is not a transient network/API error; only bounded transport retries inside one attempt are transient. While an approval hold remains unchanged, continue any independent safe non-conflicting work available under the same writer/fence, otherwise preserve the precise hold and keep monitoring enabled without cosmetic mutation or duplicate writer.

o_human_request_monitor.policy: Read the durable O user-request queue from current main and compare only against the last successful repository baseline. Notify only newly open, materially changed, or reopened requests; unchanged open, fulfilled, withdrawn, superseded, missing queue, or no-change cases do not notify. A reevaluate_by date passing is not itself a synthetic new request or notification trigger unless the authoritative queue object changes. Read-only: never mutate O or queue. Transient read failure does not advance the comparison baseline and is retried next run. Persist exact successful baseline and receipt durably.
